headline: A 2011 executive order kept certain federal advisory committees running instead of letting them expire.
what_it_does: This order continued the work of a set of federal advisory committees, which are groups that give advice to the President and federal agencies. Without action, these committees would have expired. Orders like this one are usually issued every two years and extend the committees for about two more years. The title does not list which committees were included.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the continued federal advisory committees
who_it_affects.how: They could keep serving and giving advice instead of having their committees end.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that rely on these committees
who_it_affects.how: They kept access to the outside advice these committees provide.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 30, 2011; the exact effective and end dates are not given in the title.
